Process Description:
The paper describes a discrete event simulation (DES) modeling process for improving emergency department (ED) CT access times in a large academic medical center with six unique CT machines serving multiple patient types.
Location: Saint Marys Hospital, Mayo Clinic, Rochester, Minnesota Department: Radiology - CT Scanning Resources:
        •        6 CT machines (each with different capabilities - not all can do all exam types)
        •        External transporters (shared across entire hospital)
        •        Internal transporters (dedicated to radiology only)
        •        Holding bays (waiting areas inside radiology)
Patient Types: Emergency (ED), Outpatients (scheduled), Inpatients (semi-scheduled) Volume: 10,000+ patients over 10 months Hours: 24/7 for ED/inpatients, business hours for outpatients
Current Performance:
        •        ED patient average wait: 58.8 minutes from order to scan
        •        Goal: Under 30 minutes for all ED patients
        •        National guideline for stroke: Under 25 minutes
        •        Currently achieving goal only 70% of time
Process Flow
Category 1: ED Trauma/Stroke Patients (Highest Priority)
        1        Patient arrives at emergency department with urgent condition (car accident, stroke symptoms, severe trauma)
        2        ED doctor examines patient and orders CT scan immediately
        3        System checks which CT machines are available and compatible with exam type needed
        4        Transport request sent to external transporter
        5        Transporter travels to ED, picks up patient (average: 13.6 minutes)
        6        Patient brought to CT room
        7        CT scan performed
        8        Patient returns to ED for treatment
No lab tests required - emergency fast track
Category 2: ED Non-Trauma Patients (Medium Priority)
        1        Patient arrives at emergency department (severe abdominal pain, suspected internal issues - urgent but not immediately life-threatening)
        2        ED doctor orders CT scan AND blood tests
        3        Nurse draws blood samples
        4        Blood sent to lab for testing (including creatinine test for kidney function)
        5        WAIT for lab results - creatinine test is slowest in 17% of patients (10-30+ minutes)
        6        Lab results complete and appear in computer system
        7        15-minute delay - busy ED nurse checking multiple patients, eventually notices labs are done
        8        Nurse reviews results, confirms safe for contrast dye, signals patient is cleared
        9        Transport request sent to external transporter
        10        Transporter travels to ED, picks up patient (average: 13.6 minutes)
        11        Patient brought to CT room
        12        CT scan performed (contrast dye administered)
        13        Patient returns to ED
Total average time: 61.8 minutes
Category 3: Outpatients (Lower Priority - Scheduled)
        1        Patient scheduled appointment days/weeks in advance for specific date and time
        2        Patient arrives at radiology department and checks in
        3        Staff takes patient to holding bay (preparation area inside radiology)
        4        Nurse reviews patient's pre-existing lab results and medical history (done before appointment)
        5        Nurse confirms safe for CT scan
        6        Patient waits if ED patients arrive (ED has priority)
        7        CT machine becomes available
        8        Transport request sent to internal transporter
        9        Internal transporter moves patient from holding bay to CT room (average: 7.1 minutes - shortest distance)
        10        CT scan performed
        11        Patient returns to holding bay or checks out
        12        Patient goes home
Category 4: Inpatients (Lower Priority - Semi-Scheduled)
        1        Patient already hospitalized, doctor orders CT scan
        2        Patient given time window (e.g., "between 2-4 PM today")
        3        Nurse goes to patient's hospital room, performs safety assessment
        4        Patient waits in their hospital room (could be anywhere in hospital)
        5        When time window arrives and CT machine available, transport is requested
        6        External transporter travels to patient's room location
        7        Transporter picks up patient and brings to radiology (average: 27.5 minutes - longest distance because patient could be anywhere)
        8        CT scan performed
        9        Patient transported back to hospital room
Machine Specialization
NOT all CT machines can do all exams:
        •        All 6 machines: Abdomen, chest, trauma, bones (common exams)
        •        Only 5 machines (CT1-CT5): Brain scans, vascular imaging, biopsies
        •        Only 2 machines (CT3, CT5): Cardiac (heart) scans, brain blood vessels ← BOTTLENECK
        •        Only 2 machines (CT1, CT2): Long procedures (2-5 hours each)

Process Description:
Setting: Kerem Abu Salem (KAS) security checkpoint between Israel and Gaza - humanitarian and commercial goods entry point for 2 million Gaza residents (2,000 trucks/week, 9 hours/day, 5 days/week)
Resources:
        •        4 main operational lanes (document validation, X-ray checking, cell area, Gaza staging area)
        •        41 total employees (10 validation, 9 X-ray, 14 cell area, 10 Gaza staging, various roles)
        •        11 outdoor cells (1 hectare each, 20 trucks capacity per cell)
        •        X-ray machine, dogs, hand scanners, forklifts, shuttle trucks
Operational Hours: 6 AM - 3 PM entry cutoff, 5 days/week (Sunday-Saturday), operations continue until sundown Volume: ~2,000 trucks per week (400 trucks/day average), arrival rate: 1 truck every 3 minutes Current Performance:
        •        Average cycle time: 3.05 hours/truck
        •        Average waiting time: 2.68 hours/truck
        •        Total distribution cost: $2.54M per week
Process Flow
All trucks (humanitarian and commercial) follow this process:
        1        Trucks arrive at checkpoint parking yard near entrance gates
        2        Park the truck - Wait in line to check in (average: 15 minutes)
        3        Driver walks to Israeli Authority Office to check truck number on board
        4        Driver obtains "Taom" document (describes cargo type and size)
        5        Check goods documents - Israeli security verifies Taom matches actual cargo (average: 5 minutes)
        ◦        If mismatch found (10% probability) → Truck rejected, returns to origin
        ◦        If match confirmed (90%) → Continue to next step
        6        Pay customs fees - Driver pays ~$200/truck plus other fees at designated window (average: 8 minutes)
        7        Scan the truck - Security officer randomly tests trucks using dogs and hand scanner (average: 10 minutes)
        ◦        No security concerns (85%) → Continue to cell area
        ◦        Security doubts (15%) → Diverted to X-ray machine
        8        X-ray machine scanning (for 15% of trucks) - Full truck scan (average: 15 minutes)
        ◦        Negative result (60% of scanned) → Continue to cell area
        ◦        Positive result (40% of scanned) → Search for illegal items
        9        Search for illegal items (if positive X-ray) - Forklift rearranges load (average: 30 minutes)
        ◦        Illegal items found (20%) → Truck confiscated
        ◦        No illegal items (80%) → Continue to cell area
        10        Enter Cell Area - Truck assigned to one of 11 cells (average subprocess: 45 minutes total)
        ◦        Categorize goods (food vs. non-food) by inspecting Taom (7 min)
        ◦        Unload goods from truck to cell floor (15 min)
        ◦        Security guard walks between pallets with small scan machine (8 min)
        ◦        Forklifts upload goods onto shuttle trucks (15 min)
        11        Transport to Gaza staging area - Shuttle trucks move goods (operate only between 6 AM - 3 PM, average: 10 minutes)
        12        Unload at Gaza staging area - Goods deposited (opens 3 PM - 6 PM, average: 15 minutes)
        13        Load on Palestinian trucks - Forklifts upload to Gaza-bound trucks (average: 15 minutes)
        14        Trucks depart via Philadelphia Corridor to final destinations in Gaza
Key Constraint: No direct contact between Israeli-side trucks and Gaza-side trucks (security separation)

Goal: Reduce average waiting time at security checkpoint
Parameter:
Electronic queue management system added

Process Description:
Modarres Hospital Emergency Department in Tehran, Iran operating Chest Pain Unit (CPU) for heart patients (52,000 patients/year, ~145 patients/day, 24/7 operations)
Problem: Long patient waiting times and congestion. Ministry mandates: all patients must be discharged/admitted within 6 hours of arrival. Current total average waiting time: 44 minutes, 40% have heart problems. 
Resources:
        •        1 triage nurse (categorizes patients by urgency)
        •        2 receptionists (collect patient information, locate files)
        •        3 nurses (perform ECG tests, monitoring)
        •        1 heart resident (medical decision-making, treatment)
        •        7 monitoring beds (for patient treatment and observation)
        •        CPR equipment (for most urgent cases)
Process Flow
All patients are categorized by Emergency Severity Index (ESI) from 1 (most urgent) to 5 (least urgent)
ESI Level 1: Most Urgent - Life-Threatening (2% of patients)
        1        Patient arrives by ambulance with urgent cardiac condition (cardiac arrest, severe heart attack)
        2        Immediate CPR - Patient goes directly to Cardio Pulmonary Resuscitation room (no waiting)
        3        All staff temporarily stop their tasks to provide immediate care (seconds matter)
        4        CPR performed to resuscitate patient
        5        If CPR successful → Patient transferred to CPU for further treatment
        6        If unsuccessful → Patient outcome recorded
No triage, no waiting - immediate life-saving intervention

ESI Level 2: Urgent (20% of patients)
        1        Patient arrives at ED entrance
        2        Triage assessment - Triage nurse evaluates patient (average: 2-5 minutes)
        3        Skip reception - ESI 2 patients go directly to CPU without waiting (high priority)
        4        Wait for bed assignment - Patient waits until monitoring bed becomes available
        5        Bed assigned - Patient placed on monitoring bed in CPU
        6        ECG taken - Nurse performs electrocardiography test (average: 5-15 minutes)
        7        Wait for heart resident - Patient waits for resident availability
        8        Heart resident examination - Resident evaluates condition and decides treatment (average: 10-20 minutes)
        9        Decision point:
        ◦        Treatment sufficient → Discharge from ED
        ◦        Need more treatment → Go to Step 10
        ◦        Need admission → Transfer to inpatient care unit
        10        Further treatment - Lab tests, medical advice, monitoring, another ECG (average: 45-180 minutes depending on tests)
        11        Final resident decision - Re-evaluation after treatment
        12        Patient discharged or admitted

ESI Level 3 & 4: Moderate Urgency (35% of patients)
        1        Patient arrives at ED entrance
        2        Triage assessment - Triage nurse evaluates patient (average: 2-5 minutes)
        3        Reception - Patient goes to receptionist who collects personal information and locates medical files (average: 3-5 minutes)
        4        Wait for bed assignment - Patient waits until monitoring bed available in CPU
        5        Bed assigned - Patient placed on monitoring bed
        6        ECG taken - Nurse performs test (average: 5-15 minutes)
        7        Wait for heart resident - Patient waits for resident availability
        8        Heart resident examination - Evaluation and treatment decision (average: 10-20 minutes)
        9        Decision point (same as ESI 2):
        ◦        Treatment sufficient → Discharge
        ◦        Need more treatment → Further treatment (lab tests, monitoring, etc.)
        ◦        Need admission → Transfer to inpatient unit
        10        If further treatment needed: Lab tests (45-180 min), medical advice (15-90 min), monitoring (30-60 min)
        11        Final decision - Discharge or admit

ESI Level 5: Least Urgent (43% of patients)
        1        Patient arrives at ED entrance
        2        Triage assessment - Triage nurse evaluates (average: 2-5 minutes)
        3        Reception - Collect information (average: 3-5 minutes)
        4        General physician visit - Patient sees general physician in ED (not heart specialist)
        5        Discharged - Patient leaves ED
Does NOT go to CPU - handled by general ED

Process Description:
Regional Police Traffic Directorate (RPTD) in Indonesia operates Camera-based traffic violation capture, validation, and enforcement
Staff: 7 validation officers, only 2 computers
Problem: 95%+ of 3.4 million annual violations never get validated and processed
Resources
        •        Electronic Traffic Law Enforcement (ETLE)  cameras: 24/7 violation capture
        •        2 computers for 7 officers (severe bottleneck)
        •        Event logging system
        •        SMS notification system
Process Flow (7 Steps)
Step 1: Capture → Cameras capture violation 24/7
Step 2: Validate → Officers manually validate (MUST be same day)
        •        Problem: Only 2 computers for 7 officers
        •        Result: Massive backlog; 95% violations never processed
Step 3: Sent → Confirmation letter sent to offender
Step 4: Confirm → Offender must respond within 8 days
Step 5: Billed → Payment code sent via SMS
Step 6: Blocked → Vehicle blocked if no payment within 15 days (enforcement)
Step 7: Paid → Fine paid; violation closed

Process Description:
Setting: Hungarian assembly and engineering company producing customized factory units with CNC production line (5 programmers, 6 CNC operators, 2 cutting operators, 1 technologist per shift)
Resources: 1 technologist (decision-maker), 2 cutting operators, 5 programmers (CAM program writers), 6 CNC operators (8 CNC machines available)
Process Flow
Step 1: Technologist Process Decision
Actors: 1 technologist operator per shift
Activities:
        1        Receive customer order for customized factory unit
        2        Analyze order specifications and requirements
        3        Decide sequence of required manufacturing processes
        4        Determine cutting specifications needed
        5        Decide which CAM programs required
        6        Communicate requirements to cutting plant and programming department
        7        Prioritize job sequence for production line
Duration: Variable, depends on order complexity
Step 2: Cutting Plant Process
Actors: 2 operators per shift
Activities:
        1        Receive raw material specifications from technologist
        2        Transport raw materials to cutting machine
        3        Set up cutting machine for required dimensions
        4        Cut raw materials to exact dimensions specified
        5        Transport cut materials to staging area
        6        Stack cut materials for CNC preparation
        7        Walk between machines and staging areas
        8        Document completed cuts
Duration: Per piece - 2.95 minutes for radiography equivalent (parallel activity)
Output: Raw materials cut to exact dimensions, ready for CNC milling
Non-Value-Added Activities: Walking time between cutting machine and staging area
Step 3: Programming Department - CAM Program Preparation
Actors: 5 programmers per shift
Activities - Path A (Programmers write programs):
        1        Receive CAM program requirements from technologist
        2        Analyze cutting specifications
        3        Write CAM program code for CNC machines
        4        Test program syntax and logic
        5        Save program to shared system
        6        Document program for CNC operators
        7        Wait for CNC machine availability
        8        Queue programs for machines
Activities - Path B (CNC Operators write programs - 30% of cases):
        1        CNC operators receive specifications
        2        Write CAM program at their machine
        3        Reduces available machine time
        4        Increases non-productive operator time
Output: CAM programs ready for CNC machines, either from programmers (70%) or CNC operators (30%)
Step 4: CNC Milling Plant Process
Actors: 6 operators managing 8 machines
Activities:
        1        Receive cut materials from cutting plant
        2        Transport materials to assigned CNC machine
        3        Verify CAM program availability
        4        If program not ready, WAIT (or write program themselves)
        5        Load raw material onto CNC machine
        6        Load required tools into machine tool shelf
        7        Start CNC milling program execution
        8        Monitor machine during milling
        9        Walk to other machines to check status
        10        Retrieve finished pieces from CNC machine
        11        Stack finished pieces in staging area
        12        Transport pieces to next process/quality check
        13        Clean machine and tool shelf

Goal: Increased the quantity produced per shift

Process Description:
Academic Medical Center in Amsterdam operates CT-scan facility (2 scanners, 12,000 scans/year, 8:30 AM-4:45 PM weekdays)
Problem: Current appointment-only system causes access delays (5.37 days average), requires multiple hospital visits, causes no-shows (2.6%), administrative burden. Want to enable walk-in while maintaining service for appointment-requiring patients.
Current System: All patients scheduled with appointments. 9 patient types with different requirements (77.48% eligible for walk-in, 9.96% require specific appointments, 12.56% inpatients).
Resources:
        •        2 CT scanners (CT1, CT2)
        •        Lab (capacity: 10 patients, for creatinine testing)
        •        IV preparation station (capacity: 1)
        •        Oral contrast preparation area (capacity: 10)

Process Flow (9 Patient Types)
Type 1-5: Walk-in Eligible Patients (77.48% total)
Type 1: IV(Intravenous)-Oral60 (19.09%) - Needs IV + 60-min oral contrast:
        1        Patient arrives at CT facility (walk-in)
        2        Lab visit (if no recent creatinine test - only 3% of patients, 60 min)
        3        Creatinine test check - If level too high (6% probability) → rerouted to appointment scheduler
        4        IV line placement - Nurse places IV (8.85 min average)
        5        Oral contrast drinking - Start 60 min before scan (deterministic)
        6        Wait for CT scanner availability
        7        CT scan (log-normal distribution, 4.5-40 min range)
        8        Exit
Type 2: IV-Oral30 (5.04%) - Similar to Type 1 but 30-min oral prep
Type 3: IV only (15.71%) - IV line + scan
Type 4: Oral30 (0.34%) - 30-min oral prep + scan
Type 5: Outpatient no prep (37.30%) - Direct to scan

Type 6-8: Appointment-Required Outpatients (9.96%)
Type 6: Colonography (1.23%):
        •        Requires 3-day advance preparation
        •        Reserved slots: 2-hour blocks
        •        CT time: 26.8 min average
Type 7: Puncture (1.43%):
        •        Requires anesthesia, physician present
        •        Reserved slots: 5 slots (75 min after optimization)
        •        CT time: 67.6 min average
Type 8: Cardiac (7.30%):
        •        Requires cardiologist present
        •        Reserved slots: 1 slot (15 min)
        •        CT time: varies

Type 9: Inpatients (12.56%)
        •        Arrive pre-prepared from inpatient unit
        •        Prefer same-day appointments
        •        Direct to CT scan

Process Description:
Educational Dentistry Clinic in Jordan operates Orthodontic and primary diagnosis departments (working hours: 8 AM-4 PM, 5 days/week, closed Wednesdays)

Departments: 7 private clinics (orthodontic, primary diagnosis, periodontics, restorative, surgery, kids, prosthodontics) + emergency Resources:
        •        2 receptionists (shared across all clinics)
        •        Orthodontic: 3 orthodontists, 2 treatment rooms
        •        Primary diagnosis: 3 dentists, 1 treatment room
        •        Shared: Radiography rooms (panoramic, lateral cephalometric, CT scan, digital periapical), accounting room
Patient Types: 6% new orthodontic patients, 94% follow-ups; 77% new primary diagnosis patients, 23% follow-ups
Process Flow
Orthodontic Clinic Patients
New Patients (6%):
        1        Arrive at clinic entrance
        2        Registration - Receptionist registers new patient, opens file (2.06 min average)
        3        Preliminary medical examination - Dentist examines, decides radiography type needed (7.98 min)
        4        Go to radiography room - Patient sent for panoramic + lateral cephalometric OR CT scan
        5        Radiography performed (3.92 min per type)
        6        Accounting #1 - Pay for radiography, receive receipt (1.28 min)
        7        Return to radiography - Give receipt, collect radiographs (sent via network or picked up)
        8        Return to orthodontist - Dentist diagnoses condition, begins treatment plan (10.2 min)
        9        Accounting #2 - Pay for dentist treatment
        10        Make appointment or exit - Schedule next visit or complete treatment
Follow-up Patients (94%):
        1        Arrive at clinic
        2        Registration - Confirm appointment (0.464 min)
        3        Orthodontist treatment - Direct treatment (10.2 min average, or 20-30 min for orthodontic case placement)
        4        Accounting - Pay for treatment
        5        Make appointment or exit
Special Case: Patients putting orthodontic cases (handled in morning):
        •        Priority: Highest (need 20-30 min treatment time)
        •        Current problem: Clinic schedules other patients same time → major congestion

Primary Diagnosis Clinic Patients
New Patients (77%):
        1        Arrive at clinic
        2        Registration - Open new file (2.06 min)
        3        Preliminary examination - Dentist decides radiography needed (7.98 min)
        4        Radiography - Digital periapical and/or panoramic (2.95 min)
        5        Accounting #1 - Pay for radiography
        6        Return to radiography - Collect radiographs
        7        Return to dentist - Treatment (15-25 min uniform)
        8        Accounting #2 - Pay for treatment
        9        Make appointment or exit
Follow-up Patients (23%):
        1        Registration
        2        Dentist treatment directly
        3        Accounting
        4        Exit or make appointment
